text:
alex: Noticed spike after strict-schema canary in eu-west. Fncall validation rejects jumped and a bunch of traffic got diverted to the fallback model. Example trace: `{req: xyz789, err: validation_error, path: tools[0].output, canary: strict-2026-03}`. Anyone seeing similar in other regions?

infra-bot: Metric alert: structured_validate_rejects for /chat.generate up 520% in eu-west over 5m. Canary config: strict-2026-03.

maria: Dashboard visibility is weak here 1 We only surface a single "validation" metric. We need richer labels: `reject_reason`, `schema_path`, `canary_tag`, `fallback_target`, and `tenant_id`. Also want an exemplar payload (redacted) attached so triage is fast.

hera: Agree. Also surface the current routing decision in traces so we can see whether it was routed because of reject_rate or because of manual override.

alex: Short-term mitigation thought: implement a temporary routing rule that demotes strict-validate to soft-validate when reject_rate > 2% sustained for 2m. Keep a 10m cooldown. Who implements?

sanjay: Runtime routing lives in gateway infra. I'll add a lightweight `auto_fallback_on_rejects` rule behind a feature flag. Pseudo: ```// in gateway
if (route.recent.reject_rate > 0.02 && route.canary == 'strict') {
  route.bindTo('soft-validate');
  emitLog('validation_fallback', {route, reason: 'reject_rate', window: '2m'});
}
```

jo: Caveat: switching variants affects semantics + billing. Add flags to billing pipeline to attribute tokens to original route vs fallback route. Also add a console banner per-route when it's in auto-fallback state. Customers with compliance needs must be able to opt-out.

maria: Telemetry plan: (1) add per-reject labels to metrics + export them to logs and trace spans; (2) sample 0.5% of normal requests but 100% of rejects and 5% of fallbacked requests to an eval queue; (3) store raw prompt, model output, parser stack trace, schema_path. We'll sanitize PII on ingestion. ETA: 36h for pipeline change.

alex: For rollout: gate the gateway change with a feature flag → dry-run in eu-west for 1h → enable auto-fallback at 5% traffic → 25% → monitor 24h. Need SLO adjustments so alerts don't spam during known fallback windows.

sanjay: I'll implement feature flag `route_on_reject_v2`, with a soft-kill switch `disable_auto_fallback`. Also will add `fallback_annotation` in logs and tracing when triggered. Dry-run by EOD.

hera: UI asks: add per-tenant opt-out and a global console toggle. Also add a small timeline visualization for when a route is in fallback and why (reject rate spike, manual flip, scheduled canary). This helps CS & legal.

jo: Billing: we'll attach `billing_note=fallback_route` to every token event in fallback so finance can report. Also ensure free-credits and reserved capacity handling is correct for dedicated customers.

maria: Long-term: create a "validation sandbox" in the console that runs a user's prompt set against strict vs soft schemas and shows diffed outputs and likely reject paths. RFC in a week.

alex: Good. Also need better metric names: `fncall.rejects.total`, `fncall.rejects.by_reason`, `fncall.fallbacks.count`. Make sure sampling preserves the `schema_path` dimension.

sanjay: One more infra note: when we route to soft-validate, we should keep KV-cache compatibility for the session (KV keys must be stable across variants) or we risk cache misses affecting latency. Will add compatibility check before switching.

infra-bot: Action items created: #1 gateway flag (sanjay), #2 telemetry labels & eval queue (maria), #3 console toggle + timeline (hera), #4 billing attribution (jo), #5 customer comms doc (alex). Incident channel: #inc-1726000000-schema-fallback

alex: I'll draft the comms note and tag legal/CS. Keep updates in the incident channel. Thanks team.
